Identifications on coproducts

The coproduct universal property is stated using mapping animae. To glue identifications of functors, we need the corresponding assertion for their identification animae, with the specified restriction functor. The passage between these formulations uses the decoding square from Decoding mapping animae and restriction. All categories and functors below are absolute. We write \(\star \) for whiskering, \(D(u)\) for the functor decoded from a point \(u\) of a mapping anima, and \(D_{u,v}\) for the decoding functor on identification animae.

Supplementary Lemma 1. Let \(F\colon X\to Y\) and \(G\colon X\to Z\) be functors such that \((F,G)\colon X\to Y\times Z\) is an equivalence. For \(u,v\colon T\to X\), the functor \[ (F\star -,G\star -)\colon (u=v)\longrightarrow (F\circ u=F\circ v)\times (G\circ u=G\circ v) \] is an equivalence.

Proof idea

Put \(H=(F,G)\). Postwhiskering by \(H\) is an equivalence on identification animae. Apply the product comparison to its target \((H\circ u=H\circ v)\). The two resulting components are successive postwhiskerings by \(H\) and by a projection. Associator compatibility and the projection identifications \(\pi _1\circ H=F\) and \(\pi _2\circ H=G\) compare these components with postwhiskering by \(F\) and \(G\).

Each comparison is a square with possibly different endpoints. Changing endpoints by the specified comparisons gives equivalences of the target identification animae. Pair the two squares and transfer equivalence across them. Thus it is the displayed paired postwhiskering functor itself that is an equivalence. □

Restricting to the two summands

Supplementary Lemma 2. For \(h,k\colon C\amalg D\to E\), restriction along the inclusions \(i_C\colon C\to C\amalg D\) and \(i_D\colon D\to C\amalg D\) is an equivalence \[ R_{h,k}\colon (h=k)\longrightarrow (h\circ i_C=k\circ i_C)\times (h\circ i_D=k\circ i_D), \qquad R_{h,k}=(-\star i_C,-\star i_D). \]

Proof idea

First suppose \(h=D(u)\) and \(k=D(v)\) are decoded absolute objects of \(\Map (C\amalg D,E)\). The coproduct axiom says that \[ (i_C^*,i_D^*)\colon \Map (C\amalg D,E) \longrightarrow \Map (C,E)\times \Map (D,E) \] is an equivalence. Apply Supplementary Lemma 1 to this functor and to \(u,v\). Decode the two target identification animae, using that decoding acts by equivalences.

The decoding square identifies these two components with restriction of decoded identifications, retaining the comparisons \(D(i_C^*u)=D(u)\circ i_C\) and \(D(i_D^*u)=D(u)\circ i_D\), and the corresponding comparisons for \(v\). Pair the two squares, change endpoints, and cancel the equivalence \(D_{u,v}\). This proves that \(R_{D(u),D(v)}\) is an equivalence.

For general \(h,k\), take their names in the mapping anima. The decoding comparisons give \(D(\operatorname {name}(h))=h\) and \(D(\operatorname {name}(k))=k\). Restriction commutes with changing these endpoints: prewhisker the endpoint-change square by each inclusion. Transport the decoded result across the resulting paired square to obtain the asserted equivalence \(R_{h,k}\). □

Supplementary Corollary 3. Given identifications \(\sigma \colon h\circ i_C=k\circ i_C\) and \(\tau \colon h\circ i_D=k\circ i_D\), there is an identification \(\lambda \colon h=k\) equipped with comparisons \[ \lambda \star i_C=\sigma , \qquad \lambda \star i_D=\tau . \]

Proof idea

Lift the absolute object \((\sigma ,\tau )\) along the equivalence \(R_{h,k}\) of Supplementary Lemma 2. This produces both \(\lambda \) and a comparison \(R_{h,k}(\lambda )=(\sigma ,\tau )\). Postcompose with each projection and apply the pairing projection comparisons. These are the two specified restriction comparisons. □

Keeping these comparisons makes the construction usable when gluing data with prescribed restrictions. The argument uses the mapping-anima universal property of \(C\amalg D\); it does not require the coproduct itself to be an anima.
